answer: One shed per applicant holds numbered saffron trays for 120 days, with a 150 token deposit and a 100 dollar license. Each week the keeper weighs and photographs every tray. A lab tests one gram per tray, and a neighbor signs the tally. A hollow reed in the drip basin carries a ripple gauge: still water proves the shed stayed shut, and a disturbed surface flags tampering. A forged weight forfeits the deposit and bars the keeper 180 days. Faking 10,000 sheds freezes 1,500,000 tokens and costs 1,000,000 dollars. A forger planting painted-paper bulbs pays for the field and harvests nothing.
